    Pyrifos: Contrasts with Unequal Whole-Plot Replication

    pyrifos-unequal-mixed-contrasts.Rmd

    The vegan::pyrifos experiment sampled 12 ditches repeatedly after assigning insecticide dose at the ditch level. This example keeps unequal numbers of dates and compares control with any positive dose. Ditch—not date—is the replicate for that contrast.

    data(pyrifos, package = "vegan")
ditch <- gl(12, 1, length = 132)
dose_by_ditch <- c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6)
treatment_by_ditch <- factor(
  ifelse(dose_by_ditch == 0, "control", "treated"),
  levels = c("control", "treated")
)
dates_per_ditch <- c(3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6)
occasion <- ave(seq_len(nrow(pyrifos)), ditch, FUN = seq_along)
keep <- occasion <= dates_per_ditch[ditch]

community <- pyrifos[keep, ]
environment <- data.frame(
  ditch = droplevels(ditch[keep]),
  treatment = treatment_by_ditch[ditch[keep]]
)
table(table(environment$ditch),
      tapply(environment$treatment, environment$ditch, unique))
#>    
#>     1 2
#>   3 1 2
#>   4 1 2
#>   5 1 2
#>   6 1 2

    The contrast operates on equally weighted ditch centroids. Residuals can move only among ditches with the same retained observation count; the compiler rejects if those size strata cannot span the treatment contrast.

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | ditch),
  environment,
  vegdist(community, method = "bray")
)

fit <- permanova_mixed_contrasts(
  design,
  contrasts = c(control = -1, treated = 1),
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260720
)
fit
#> Mixed-design distance contrasts
#> Design: unequally replicated random intercept 
#> Estimand: equally weighted random-intercept unit centroids 
#> Denominator: MS[unit-centroid Residual] 
#>    contrast                                         estimand df         ss
#>  contrast_1 equally weighted random-intercept unit centroids  1 0.05544497
#>                 denominator denominator_df pseudo_f p_perm p_adjusted
#>  MS[unit-centroid Residual]             10 1.419671   0.13       0.13
#>  adjustment
#>        holm
    with(fit$tests[[1]], list(
  estimand = estimand,
  denominator = denominator$expression,
  exchangeable_units = exchangeable_units,
  permutation_strata = permutation_strata,
  permutation_algorithm = permutation_algorithm
))
#> $estimand
#> [1] "equally weighted random-intercept unit centroids"
#> 
#> $denominator
#> [1] "MS[unit-centroid Residual]"
#> 
#> $exchangeable_units
#> [1] "ditch"
#> 
#> $permutation_strata
#> [1] "exact random-intercept unit observation count"
#> 
#> $permutation_algorithm
#> [1] "contrast-specific Freedman-Lane permutation of whole random-intercept units within exact size strata"

    With two treatment levels this planned comparison is also the only pairwise comparison. Designs with more treatment levels can use permanova_mixed_pairwise() and Holm adjustment. Unbalanced nested designs use top-unit centroids within identical topology strata; incomplete randomized blocks use observed cell centroids, additive block adjustment, and block-by-cell-size strata.
